review: 5:1–5:2 אַתָּה הַלֶּחֶם ... הָאֱמֶת וְהַחַיִּים — John 6:35 and 14:6; the Arabic الْقُوتُ وَالطَّرِيقُ / الْحَقُّ وَالْحَيَاة is the same pair of sayings, and the Hebrew keeps the 'I am' predicate without adding אֲנִי (which would break the metre).
5:3 הַמְּתַוֵּךְ — 'the Mediator' (1 Tim 2:5, מְתַוֵּךְ is post-biblical but fixed in liturgical Hebrew); the Arabic الْوَسِيط is that office, not a mere 'middle man'.
3:3–3:4 לֹא־יִזָּכֵר הֶחֵטְא — 'sin shall not be remembered' (Jer 31:34, מֵחַטָּאתָם לֹא אֶזְכָּר־עוֹד); the Arabic فَلَا ذِكْرَ لِلْخَطَايَا is that promise.
4:3 זָרַם חַסְדְּךָ כַּנָּהָר — 'Your grace streamed like the river'; the Arabic فَاضَ ('overflowed') has no single biblical equivalent, and זָרַם is the verb of water rushing (Hab 3:10).
